thread:
maya: quick eyeball needed on the "slimline" capacity toolbar I've been iterating on. goal: make the card readable at 1200px and on smaller dashboard tiles. current pieces: min/max steppers, burst toggle (with details), pool chip, SLO slider, live-cost badge. feels cramped and tab heavy. thinking: a two-tier compact layout where primary controls (min/max, burst) live inline, and secondary details (burst detail, pool metadata, cost breakdown) live in a detachable panel/popover. open to other patterns.
jordan: i like the two-tier approach. question: should the detachable panel be transient (popover) or persistent (drawer) when expanded? transient keeps dashboard tidy; persistent could be used for advanced editing. maybe transient by default, persistent with an "open for editing" affordance. i'll mock both. :art: 
liam: engineering constraints: transient popover with proper focus management is easiest. persistent drawer requires routing state and undo considerations. for popover, ensure aria-controls + aria-expanded on the toggle and that Esc returns focus. also watch for stacking context if the card is inside a scroll container.
olivia: UX: make burst discoverable even in compact mode. suggestion: show a tiny badge on the burst toggle like "+Burst" and include a first-run inline hint. add a subtle pulsing ring on first exposure (only once). also recommend numeric inline readouts for min/max next to stepper controls for quick scanning.
maya: good call. also want SLO slider to expose the numeric value next to the handle while dragging and to announce changes to SRs. color contrast for the filled track needs verifying.
jordan: minor copy thoughts: rename "Burst" to "Temporary burst" or even "Burst (temp)" for brevity in small chip widths. live-cost badge copy should be short, maybe "~$0.12/hr" — avoid verbs. localization note: keep these under ~40 chars.
alex: implementation notes: keep DOM order matching the tab order for predictability. suggested tab order: min -> max -> burst -> pool -> slo -> cost. use the following small helpers:
```
.stepper button { min-width:40px; min-height:40px; }
.popover[role="dialog"] { outline: none; }
```
For SR announcement on slider changes, use aria-live="polite" region updated by JS instead of relying solely on aria-valuenow on the input.
liam: dev note: when the popover is open, trap focus inside it and set inert on the background region if possible. will estimate effort once we choose transient vs persistent.
maya: action items: jordan to post compact+expanded mocks and annotate a11y points; alex to add keyboard and SR patterns to the dev notes; liam to prototype focus-trap approach and report back with ETA; olivia to write two short copy variants for "burst" and the cost badge. i'll open a small ticket for the pattern and link the mocks.
design-bot: created ticket <https://redwood.app/t/RED-4720|RED-4720> "Slimline capacity toolbar: compact two-tier pattern, a11y + keyboard" :white_check_mark:
jordan: i'll upload mocks by EOD and include a short a11y checklist. @maya ping me on the file when ready for review. :thumbsup: 
maya: thanks team, let's aim to reuse this pattern on other compact cards if it works.
